name: Buch in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Luxurious residential community in the Inntal valley between Jenbach and Schwaz, offering breathtaking views of the Zillertaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Buch in Tirol is a welcoming and historically significant municipality in the Schwaz district, located at an altitude of approximately 545 meters in the Lower Inn Valley south of the Inn River. Home to around 2,640 residents across nearly ten square kilometers, the village lies in the direct vicinity of the silver mining town of Schwaz and opposite the transit hub of Jenbach. The municipality encompasses the districts of Maurach, Buch, St. Margarethen, Rotholz, and Troi. Formerly known as Buch bei Jenbach, it was officially renamed Buch in Tirol in 2010. Positioned within the Karwendel Silver Region, it combines nationally celebrated monuments, lush nature, and a distinguished agricultural heritage.

History

The settlement was first recorded in 1120 in monastic records from St. Georgenberg as Puech, derived from a beech forest, honored by a red beech tree on the municipal coat of arms. The village gained historical prominence through Rottenburg Castle, erected around 1149 as the ancestral seat of the powerful Counts of Rottenburg, the wealthiest feudal lords in medieval Tyrol. Following the Rottenburg Feud of 1410 against Duke Frederick IV, the stronghold was besieged and dismantled, leaving the atmospheric ruins seen today. The castle is famously connected with Saint Notburga (ca. 1265–1313), Tyrol's most revered folk saint, who served as a pious maidservant here; in 1956, the Saint Notburga Chapel was built amidst the ruins featuring the Staircase of Reconciliation. Another architectural gem is Schloss Rotholz, a Renaissance hunting palace built between 1575 and 1585 by Archduke Ferdinand II for his consort Philippine Welser, now home to a prestigious state agricultural college. The parish church of Saint Margaret in St. Margarethen, perched on a scenic hill, was expanded in Late Gothic style to serve incoming silver miners.

How to Get There

Motorists access Buch via the Inntal motorway A12, exiting at Jenbach or Schwaz, and following federal highway B171 or provincial road L218 in minutes. Rail passengers benefit from immediate proximity to Jenbach railway station, an international ICE, Railjet, and Nightjet stop situated directly on the opposite bank of the Inn and accessible via the footbridge. Frequent regional VVT bus route 4111 connects Schwaz, Buch, and Jenbach.

Tips

A top cultural highlight is the hike to the Rottenburg Castle ruins with the Notburga Chapel and the towering fifty-meter Notburga Spruce, a protected natural monument. The romantic Bucher Waterfall Trail guides walkers along wooden walkways to an observation platform overlooking roaring cascades. Food connoisseurs should visit the farm shop of the Rotholz Agricultural College, acclaimed across western Austria for its award-winning alpine cheeses and artisan sheep milk cheeses. Cyclists can pedal along the scenic Inn River Cycle Path R1 running right through the municipality.
